chunks: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah, and sufficient is your Lord as Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants.
ai.seo_question: How many generations did God destroy after Noah according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution against those who reject prophetic guidance, linking the destruction of past generations to the specific context of the Prophet's night journey. It serves as a reassurance to the Prophet that God’s omniscience ('Khabeeran Basheeran') guarantees justice even when the disbelievers remain unscathed in the short term.
